_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for AAPL retrospectives (retro/build_aapl.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern); every Apple earnings release of the period came after the close. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), each field of the latest guide for the current fiscal year published by AS_OF, and events published since that vintage. Apple's fiscal year is the 52 or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September. Values are as reported (GAAP), per share on the basis of the filing that published them; a vintage takes each year from the latest 10-K that reports it, and eps_published / shares_published give such a year's own publication date, so a stock split ('splits') restates exactly the per-share facts published before its effective date. Apple guides one quarter at a time: each release gives the next quarter's revenue (a dollar level) and diluted EPS, read as growth against the same quarter a year earlier (prior_sales_b, from that quarter's own release); no release or filing of the period gives a full-year revenue, EPS or operating-margin guide. A 10-Q's or 10-K's gross-margin expectation (gm_pct for a quarter, gm_guide_pct for a fiscal year) is shown in the guide line and feeds no input. A print's margins and growth rates are derived from the published income statement and data sheet (the raw figures are in its notes); non_mac_pct is the growth of net sales less Mac (CPU) net sales. rule_t holds the ten annual values (FY1998-FY2007) behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing. A filing that re-presents a 10-K is a vintage of its own: the FY2009 10-K/A of 2010-01-26 revises FY2007-FY2009 for the accounting principles Apple adopted retrospectively in Q1 FY10, and amends Items 6-8 only, so its business wording is the FY2009 10-K's. A guide's prior_sales_b is the same quarter a year earlier on the guide's own accounting basis, from the latest filing published by the guide's date that reports it (the revised FY2009 quarters for the guides of fiscal 2010). From FY2009 a print's lt_securities_b holds the long-term marketable securities (display only); from Q1 FY10 a print has no iPhone and Apple TV deferral (deferred_iphone_b null); ipad_units_k from Q3 FY10.

rule_t._doc: Rule T (retro/README.md, LOW and AAPL): for each signal its ten annual values FY1998-FY2007, each change from the latest 10-K published by 2008-01-04 that reports both years (a company-published figure excluding items replaces the reported one where a filing publishes it for both years); XBULL = the best year, BULL = the median, BASE = the worst year, BEAR = one median-to-worst step below the worst; rounded half up to whole percent or 10 bp
